key: I have beheld his strong and secret dwelling, longing have sought the Founder’s habitation. I asked of others, and they said in answer, May we, awakened men, attain to Indra.
s: After the opening question, who has seen Indra, the singer recounts his search; Sāyaṇa, on 5.30.2, takes him as a seer who asked whether Indra, though real, was hard to reach and, told he was easy, saw the rest of the hymn for reaching him.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.30.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 398838 (2023)

evidence.gloss: I asked others too, the learned on the way, about Indra. Asked, they told me of Indra. What they said: we, leaders of rites, seeking to know, have attained Indra. The meaning is: though Indra exists, if he is hard to reach he is not to be approached; wishing to know this, the seer asked about his nature, and, told by those he asked that he is easy to reach, he saw the rest of the hymn for reaching Indra.

reason: The problem holds: ‘reads it as a seeker’ made the search (‘it’) a person, and ‘sees the rest of the hymn’ stood without the seer who sees it. Re-opened packet.js veda 50 --verse 5.30.2: Sāyaṇa closes ‘yadyapīndro vidyate tathāpi durlabhaś ced anupagantavyaḥ iti bubhutsamānaḥ svabhāvam apṛcchat pṛṣṭaiś ca sulabhaḥ ity ukta indraprāptyarthaṃ sūktaśeṣam apaśyat’: wishing to know whether Indra, though he exists, is hard to reach and so not to be approached, he asked; told by those asked that Indra is easy to reach, he saw the rest of the hymn for reaching Indra. The rewrite takes the singer (‘him’) as a seer, so ‘saw the rest of the hymn’ is the seer’s seeing; ‘hard to reach’ renders durlabha more closely than the critic’s ‘beyond reach’, and ‘saw … for reaching him’ keeps his apaśyat and indraprāptyartham where the critic’s ‘was granted’ would add a giver his words do not name. Key, ref, at, src and evidence unchanged; in the plain sense only ‘tells of’ became ‘recounts’, to keep the sentence at 45 words. verse.js ok (5.30.2, [383,2]); entry-check ok.
